records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: Yahweh spoke: the first of the instructions given to Moses on the mountain
decisions.reason: Moses has gone up into the cloud on the mountain and stays there forty days and forty nights (24:15-18). What God says there runs from here to 31:17, in a series of speeches that each open in much the same way (30:11, 17, 22, 34; 31:1, 12). Then God gives Moses the two tablets (31:18). The first speech, from 25:2 to 30:10, describes the tabernacle, its furnishings and the priests who serve in it.

records.heading: Contributions for the sanctuary

records.source: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְיִקְחוּ־לִ֖י תְּרוּמָ֑ה מֵאֵ֤ת כָּל־אִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִדְּבֶ֣נּוּ לִבּ֔וֹ תִּקְח֖וּ אֶת־תְּרוּמָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel, and let them take for me a contribution; from with every man whom moves him his heart you will take my contribution.
pieces: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and have them set aside a contribution for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You are to receive {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} contribution from {{gender:everyone|every man}} whose heart moves {{gender:them|him}} to give.

L.2: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, that they take for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a heave offering; from {{gender:every one|every man}} whose heart makes {{gender:them|him}} willing you shall take {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heave offering.

R.2: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a special gift. Receive {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} gift from everyone who wants to give it.

decisions.choice: contribution: something lifted off and set apart from what one has, as a gift for God
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "to lift, raise". It is a portion taken from a person's goods and given over to God for his use. It is used of gifts for the sanctuary (35:5, 21, 24) and of portions of sacrifices given to the priests (29:27-28). The older rendering "heave offering" comes from the idea of lifting.

decisions.choice: whose heart moves him: who gives freely, of his own will
decisions.reason: The verb means to make willing or to move to give freely. The gifts are not a tax; they come from those who want to give. The same verb is used when the people bring their gifts in 35:21, 29, where "men and women" both give (35:22, 29). The word for "freewill offering" comes from the same root.

decisions.choice: they take ... you shall take: the people set the gifts apart, and Moses and his helpers receive them
decisions.reason: The people "take" the contribution from what they have, and "you" (plural, Moses and those with him) "take" it from them, that is, receive it.

decisions.choice: {{gender:everyone|every man}} whose heart moves {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: "Every man" here means each person, and 35:22, 29 show that men and women both gave. The gender setting gives the inclusive wording by default and the traditional "every man ... him" as the alternative. Readable says "everyone who wants to give", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: contribution (Balanced); special gift (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional "heave offering". Balanced says "contribution", the word used throughout the tabernacle chapters; Readable says "special gift".

records.source: וְזֹאת֙ הַתְּרוּמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּקְח֖וּ מֵאִתָּ֑ם זָהָ֥ב וָכֶ֖סֶף וּנְחֹֽשֶׁת׃
records.gloss: And this [is] the contribution which you will take from with them: gold and silver and bronze,
pieces: This is the contribution you are to receive from them: gold, silver and bronze,

L.3: And this [is] the heave offering which you shall take from them: gold and silver and bronze,

R.3: Here are the gifts you may accept from them: gold, silver, and bronze.

decisions.choice: bronze: copper or an alloy of copper
decisions.reason: The word covers copper and its alloys. In the tabernacle it is used for the altar of burnt offering, the basin, and the bases and pegs of the courtyard (27:2-6, 19; 30:18).

decisions.choice: gold, silver and bronze: metals in order of worth
decisions.reason: The list moves from the most precious metal to the least. In the tabernacle the most precious materials are used closest to the most holy place: gold for the ark, the table and the lampstand inside, bronze for the altar in the courtyard outside. Much of this metal came from what the Egyptians gave Israel (3:22; 12:35-36).

records.source: וּתְכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ וְעִזִּֽים׃
records.gloss: and violet and purple and worm of scarlet and fine linen and goats,
pieces: blue, purple and scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats' hair,

L.4: and blue and purple and scarlet [yarn], and fine linen, and goats' [hair],

R.4: They may also give blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, fine linen, and goats' hair.

decisions.choice: blue, purple and scarlet: wool dyed in costly colors
decisions.reason: The first two colors were made from shellfish dye, the first a violet-blue and the second a red-purple; both were costly and were worn by the rich and by kings. "Scarlet" is literally "worm of scarlet": a deep red dye made from an insect. The words name the colored yarn or cloth, most likely wool, used for the curtains and the priests' garments (26:1, 31; 28:5-6).

decisions.choice: fine linen: cloth woven from flax of high quality
decisions.reason: This is the fine white linen Joseph was dressed in when Pharaoh honored him (Genesis 41:42). Linen made of flax was a well-known product of Egypt.

decisions.choice: goats: goats' hair
decisions.reason: The word is simply "goats"; the material meant is their hair, spun into yarn by the women (35:26) and woven into the curtains of the tent over the tabernacle (26:7).

decisions.choice: yarn ... goats' hair
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names only the colors and "goats". Balanced and Readable add "yarn" and "hair", which the context requires; Literal brackets them. Readable starts a new sentence, "They may also give", to break up the long list.

records.source: וְעֹרֹ֨ת אֵילִ֧ם מְאָדָּמִ֛ים וְעֹרֹ֥ת תְּחָשִׁ֖ים וַעֲצֵ֥י שִׁטִּֽים׃
records.gloss: and skins of rams dyed red and skins of tahash and woods of acacia,
pieces: rams' skins dyed red, fine leather, acacia wood,

L.5: and skins of rams dyed red, and skins of fine leather, and acacia wood,

R.5: They may give rams' skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood.

decisions.choice: skins of a kind not certainly known: a fine leather
decisions.reason: The word that describes these skins is not certainly known. It names either an animal or a kind of leather. The skins formed the outermost covering of the tabernacle (26:14) and were used to wrap its holy things on the march (Numbers 4:6-14); in Ezekiel 16:10 sandals are made of them. Some connect the word with an animal of the Red Sea such as the dugong (sea cow) or the dolphin; older versions such as the King James Version said "badgers' skins"; others take it as a word for a fine, specially treated leather or for a color. What is clear is that it was a durable, valuable leather.

decisions.choice: rams' skins dyed red: tanned rams' leather colored red
decisions.reason: The skins of rams, tanned and dyed red, made the covering that lay over the goats' hair tent (26:14).

decisions.choice: acacia wood: the hard wood of the acacia tree
decisions.reason: The acacia grows in the dry country of Sinai and the Jordan valley. Its wood is hard and resists decay, and it is the wood used for the ark, the table, the altars and the frames of the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: fine leather
decisions.reason: The animal or material is uncertain (m1), so every level says "fine leather" and does not choose between the suggested animals; a footnote gives the alternatives. Readable keeps the list in its own sentence.

records.source: שֶׁ֖מֶן לַמָּאֹ֑ר בְּשָׂמִים֙ לְשֶׁ֣מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָ֔ה וְלִקְטֹ֖רֶת הַסַּמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: oil for the light, spices for [the] oil of the anointing and for [the] incense of the fragrances,
pieces: oil for the lamps, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense,

L.6: oil for the light, spices for the oil of anointing and for the incense of fragrances,

R.6: They may give olive oil for the lamps, and spices for the oil used to anoint and for the sweet-smelling incense.

decisions.choice: oil for the light: olive oil for the lamps
decisions.reason: The oil is the pure olive oil burned in the lamps of the lampstand (27:20; Leviticus 24:2).

decisions.choice: the anointing oil and the incense: made from spices by a set recipe
decisions.reason: The recipes for the holy anointing oil and the incense are given in 30:22-38. The oil set apart the tabernacle, its furnishings and the priests; the incense was burned on the gold altar (30:7-8).

decisions.choice: lamps
decisions.reason: "The light" means the lamps of the lampstand (verse 37; 27:20); Balanced and Readable say "lamps". Readable also names the oil as olive oil, as 27:20 does.

records.source: אַבְנֵי־שֹׁ֕הַם וְאַבְנֵ֖י מִלֻּאִ֑ים לָאֵפֹ֖ד וְלַחֹֽשֶׁן׃
records.gloss: stones of onyx and stones of setting for the ephod and for the breastpiece.
pieces: and onyx stones and other stones to be set in the ephod and the breastpiece.

L.7: stones of onyx and stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece.

R.7: And they may give onyx stones and other precious stones to be mounted on the ephod and the breastpiece.

decisions.choice: onyx: a precious stone, not certainly identified
decisions.reason: The stone is named with gold in the land of Havilah (Genesis 2:12). Two of them, engraved with the names of the tribes, are set on the shoulders of the ephod (28:9-12). It is probably onyx, but some take it to be carnelian or another stone.

decisions.choice: stones of setting: gems to be mounted in settings
decisions.reason: The phrase means stones for filling settings, that is, gems mounted in gold. The twelve stones of the breastpiece are set this way (28:17-20).

decisions.choice: the ephod and the breastpiece: garments of the high priest
decisions.reason: Both are described in chapter 28: the ephod, an apron-like vestment (28:6-14), and the breastpiece worn over it (28:15-30).

decisions.choice: other (precious) stones
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "other stones" to show these are gems besides the onyx.

records.source: וְעָ֥שׂוּ לִ֖י מִקְדָּ֑שׁ וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֖י בְּתוֹכָֽם׃
records.gloss: And let them make for me a sanctuary, and I will dwell in [the] midst of them.
pieces: They are to make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a sanctuary, so that I may dwell among them.

L.8: And they shall make for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a sanctuary, and I will dwell in their midst.

R.8: Have the people make a holy place for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so that I can live among them.

decisions.choice: sanctuary: a holy place, set apart for God
decisions.reason: The word comes from the root for "holy". It names the whole tabernacle as the place that belongs to God.

decisions.choice: I will dwell among them: God's purpose is to live with his people
decisions.reason: The verb means to settle or dwell, and the word for "tabernacle" in the next verse comes from it: the tabernacle is the place of God's dwelling. The aim of the whole building is stated here and again in 29:45-46: God will live among the Israelites and be their God. Leviticus 26:11-12 and Ezekiel 37:27 return to the same promise.

decisions.choice: and I will dwell: the purpose of the making
decisions.reason: The two clauses are joined by "and". The second gives the reason for the first: they are to make the sanctuary so that God may dwell among them.

decisions.choice: holy place ... live
decisions.reason: Readable says "holy place" for "sanctuary" and "live" for "dwell". "The people" names who is to make it.

records.source: כְּכֹ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִי֙ מַרְאֶ֣ה אוֹתְךָ֔ אֵ֚ת תַּבְנִ֣ית הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת תַּבְנִ֣ית כָּל־כֵּלָ֑יו וְכֵ֖ן תַּעֲשֽׂוּ׃ס
records.gloss: According to all that I [am] showing you, the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its articles, and so you will make [it].
pieces: You are to make it in keeping with everything I show you, following the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its furnishings.

L.9: According to all that I am showing you, the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its articles, so you shall make [it].

R.9: I will show you a plan for the tabernacle, the sacred tent, and for everything in it. Make all of it just the way I show you.

decisions.choice: pattern: a model or plan of the thing to be built
decisions.reason: The word means a form or design, sometimes a model of something. David gives Solomon the "pattern" of the temple (1 Chronicles 28:11-19). Here it is something God shows Moses, either a model or a vision; the text does not say which. Hebrews 8:5 quotes verse 40 and calls the earthly tabernacle a copy and shadow of the heavenly one.

decisions.choice: tabernacle: the dwelling place, God's tent
decisions.reason: The word means "dwelling place" and comes from the verb "dwell" in verse 8. It names the tent God will live in among his people, and sometimes the inner tent of curtains within it (26:1).

decisions.choice: I am showing you: what God is about to show, or is showing, Moses
decisions.reason: The verb is a participle, which can describe something happening now or about to happen. Verse 40 uses the same form: "which you are being shown on the mountain".

decisions.choice: the tabernacle, the sacred tent
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "tabernacle" and adds "the sacred tent" to explain it. It says "plan" for "pattern" and turns the verse into two short sentences.

decisions.choice: furnishings
decisions.reason: The "articles" of the tabernacle are its furniture and utensils; Balanced says "furnishings". Literal keeps "articles".

records.source: וְעָשׂ֥וּ אֲר֖וֹן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And they will make an ark of woods of acacia, two cubits and a half its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height.
pieces: They are to make an ark of acacia wood, {{units:about 3 3/4 feet|2 1/2 cubits}} long, {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} wide and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} high.

L.10: And they shall make an ark of acacia wood; 2 1/2 cubits [shall be] its length, and 1 1/2 cubits its breadth, and 1 1/2 cubits its height.

R.10: Have them make an ark out of acacia wood. It is the ark that will hold the covenant tablets. It must be {{units:about 3 3/4 feet|2 1/2 cubits}} long, {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} wide, and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} high.

decisions.choice: ark: a chest or box
decisions.reason: The word means a chest. It is used of Joseph's coffin (Genesis 50:26) and of the money chest in the temple (2 Kings 12:10). It is not the word used for Noah's ark. This chest will hold the tablets of the covenant (verse 16) and is often called "the ark of the testimony" (verse 22) or "the ark of the covenant" (Numbers 10:33).

decisions.choice: cubit: the length from elbow to fingertip, about 18 inches (45 centimeters)
decisions.reason: The cubit was the common measure of length, the length of a man's forearm. The ark is 2 1/2 cubits long and 1 1/2 cubits wide and high: about 45 by 27 by 27 inches (about 113 by 68 by 68 centimeters). A longer royal cubit of about 21 inches was also used in the ancient Near East, so the figures are approximate.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 3 3/4 feet|2 1/2 cubits}} ... {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measures in feet by default, rounded, with "about", and the units setting shows the original "cubits". Literal always keeps the original unit. Numerals are used in measurements.

decisions.choice: the ark that will hold the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "ark" and adds a sentence saying what it is for, since "ark" now usually means a large boat: it will hold the tablets of the covenant (verse 16). Later verses say "the ark".

records.heading: The ark

records.source: וְצִפִּיתָ֤ אֹתוֹ֙ זָהָ֣ב טָה֔וֹר מִבַּ֥יִת וּמִח֖וּץ תְּצַפֶּ֑נּוּ וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ עָלָ֛יו זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And you will overlay it [with] gold pure, from inside and from outside you will overlay it, and you will make on it a molding of gold all around.
pieces: Overlay it with pure gold on the inside and the outside, and put a gold molding around it on every side.

L.11: And you shall overlay it [with] pure gold; inside and outside you shall overlay it, and you shall make on it a molding of gold all around.

R.11: Cover it with pure gold, inside and outside, and put a gold border all around it.

decisions.choice: overlay: cover with a thin layer of metal
decisions.reason: The wood is plated with gold. The same verb is used of the table (verse 24), the frames (26:29) and the altars (27:2; 30:3).

decisions.choice: molding: a raised border or rim
decisions.reason: The word means a border, perhaps a crown-like rim, running around the chest. It is used only of the ark, the table and the incense altar (verse 24; 30:3). Where on the ark it ran, whether around the top edge or the middle, the text does not say.

decisions.choice: pure gold: refined gold
decisions.reason: "Pure" marks gold that has been refined, used for the things nearest God's presence: the ark, the mercy seat, the table and the lampstand.

records.source: וְיָצַ֣קְתָּ לּ֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב וְנָ֣תַתָּ֔ה עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל־צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּעֹ֔ת עַל־צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃
records.gloss: And you will cast for it four rings of gold, and you will put [them] on its four feet, and two rings on its one side, and two rings on its second side.
pieces: Cast four rings of gold for it and fix them at its four feet, so that each side has two rings.

L.12: And you shall cast for it four rings of gold and put [them] on its four feet, and two rings on its one side and two rings on its second side.

R.12: Cast four gold rings and attach them near its four feet, two rings on each side.

decisions.choice: cast: pour molten metal into a mold
decisions.reason: The rings are made by pouring melted gold into molds.

decisions.choice: feet: the lower corners of the chest
decisions.reason: The word usually means a foot or a step. Here it most likely means the four lower corners on which the chest stands, or small feet at those corners. The rings are placed low, so that the chest rides high when it is carried.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ בַדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And you will make poles of woods of acacia and you will overlay them [with] gold.
pieces: You are also to make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.

L.13: And you shall make poles of acacia wood and overlay them [with] gold.

R.13: Make poles out of acacia wood, and cover them with gold.

decisions.choice: poles: carrying poles
decisions.reason: Long poles passed through the rings so that the ark could be carried on the shoulders of the Levites (Numbers 7:9; 1 Chronicles 15:15).

records.source: וְהֵֽבֵאתָ֤ אֶת־הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן לָשֵׂ֥את אֶת־הָאָרֹ֖ן בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will bring the poles in the rings on [the] sides of the ark, to carry the ark by them.
pieces: Slide the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark, so that the ark can be carried by them.

L.14: And you shall bring the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark by them.

R.14: Put the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark. Use them to carry the ark.

decisions.choice: to carry the ark by them: the ark is carried, not handled
decisions.reason: The ark was holy, and those who carried it were not to touch it (Numbers 4:15). When Uzzah took hold of it, he died (2 Samuel 6:6-7).

records.source: בְּטַבְּעֹת֙ הָאָרֹ֔ן יִהְי֖וּ הַבַּדִּ֑ים לֹ֥א יָסֻ֖רוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: In [the] rings of the ark will be the poles; not will they be removed from it.
pieces: The poles are to be kept in the rings of the ark and never pulled out.

L.15: In the rings of the ark the poles shall be; they shall not be removed from it.

R.15: The poles must stay in the rings of the ark. Do not take them out.

decisions.choice: not to be removed: the poles stay in the rings at all times
alternatives: the poles are not to be taken out while the ark is being carried
decisions.reason: The poles stayed in place even when the ark was at rest, so it was always ready to be carried and never needed to be handled. In Solomon's temple the poles were still in place and could be seen from the holy place (1 Kings 8:8). Numbers 4:6 speaks of putting the poles in place when the ark is wrapped for the journey; this may mean adjusting them, since this verse says they were never taken out.

records.source: וְנָתַתָּ֖ אֶל־הָאָרֹ֑ן אֵ֚ת הָעֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶתֵּ֖ן אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And you will put into the ark the testimony which I will give to you.
pieces: Inside the ark you are to place the testimony that I will give you.

L.16: And you shall put into the ark the testimony which I will give you.

R.16: Put the covenant tablets that I will give you inside the ark.

decisions.choice: the testimony: the stone tablets of the covenant
decisions.reason: The "testimony" is the two stone tablets with the Ten Words written on them, which bear witness to the covenant God made with Israel. They are called "the two tablets of the testimony" (31:18; 32:15), and the ark that holds them is "the ark of the testimony" (verse 22). God promised Moses these tablets in 24:12; Moses puts them in the ark in 40:20.

decisions.choice: the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: Readable says what the testimony is: the tablets of the covenant. Literal and Balanced keep "the testimony".

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ כַפֹּ֖רֶת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר אַמָּתַ֤יִם וָחֵ֨צִי֙ אָרְכָּ֔הּ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי רָחְבָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And you will make a mercy seat [of] gold pure, two cubits and a half its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth.
pieces: Make a mercy seat of pure gold, {{units:about 3 3/4 feet|2 1/2 cubits}} long and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} wide.

L.17: And you shall make a mercy seat of pure gold; 2 1/2 cubits [shall be] its length, and 1 1/2 cubits its breadth.

R.17: Make the lid of the ark out of pure gold. It is the place where sins are covered. It must be {{units:about 3 3/4 feet|2 1/2 cubits}} long and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} wide.

decisions.choice: mercy seat: the gold lid of the ark, the place where atonement is made
decisions.reason: The word comes from the root used for "make atonement" (30:10, 15-16), and it names the solid gold lid laid on the ark (verse 21). It is more than a cover. Once a year, on the Day of Atonement, the high priest sprinkled blood on it and before it to make atonement for himself and the people (Leviticus 16:2, 13-16), and the room that held the ark could be called "the house of the mercy seat" (1 Chronicles 28:11). God speaks from above it (verse 22; Numbers 7:89). The ancient Greek translation calls it the place of atonement, and the New Testament uses that word in Romans 3:25 and Hebrews 9:5. The lid is also where God is present, enthroned above the cherubim (1 Samuel 4:4; Psalm 99:1); it is not a seat to sit on.

decisions.choice: mercy seat
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the traditional name "mercy seat", which goes back to William Tyndale's translation of 1530 and which readers know and which points to what the lid is for. A footnote gives "atonement cover" and "place of atonement" (m1).

decisions.choice: the lid of the ark ... the place where sins are covered
decisions.reason: Readable says what the mercy seat is, the lid of the ark, and adds a sentence on its purpose: it is where atonement is made, where sins are covered (Leviticus 16:14-16). Later verses call it "the lid".

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֛יתָ שְׁנַ֥יִם כְּרֻבִ֖ים זָהָ֑ב מִקְשָׁה֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם מִשְּׁנֵ֖י קְצ֥וֹת הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת׃
records.gloss: And you will make two cherubim [of] gold; hammered work you will make them, from [the] two ends of the mercy seat.
pieces: Make two cherubim of gold. Make them of hammered work, at the two ends of the mercy seat.

L.18: And you shall make two cherubim [of] gold; [of] hammered work you shall make them, at the two ends of the mercy seat.

R.18: Make two cherubim out of hammered gold for the two ends of the lid. Cherubim are winged heavenly creatures.

decisions.choice: cherubim: winged heavenly beings who guard God's holy presence
decisions.reason: Cherubim guard the way to the tree of life (Genesis 3:24), and God is spoken of as enthroned above the cherubim (1 Samuel 4:4; 2 Samuel 6:2; Psalm 99:1). Ezekiel describes them with wings and faces (Ezekiel 10). Here two gold figures of them stand on the mercy seat, and figures of them are woven into the curtains (26:1, 31). The text does not describe their form beyond their wings and faces (verse 20).

decisions.choice: hammered work: beaten from a single piece of metal
decisions.reason: The cherubim are not cast and attached; they are beaten out of the same piece of gold as the mercy seat (verse 19). The lampstand is made the same way (verses 31, 36).

decisions.choice: Cherubim are winged heavenly creatures.
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "cherubim" and adds a sentence to say what they are; their wings are described in verse 20.

records.source: וַ֠עֲשֵׂה כְּר֨וּב אֶחָ֤ד מִקָּצָה֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וּכְרוּב־אֶחָ֥ד מִקָּצָ֖ה מִזֶּ֑ה מִן־הַכַּפֹּ֛רֶת תַּעֲשׂ֥וּ אֶת־הַכְּרֻבִ֖ים עַל־שְׁנֵ֥י קְצוֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And make one cherub from [the] end on this [side], and one cherub from [the] end on that [side]; from the mercy seat you will make the cherubim on its two ends.
pieces: Form one cherub at this end and another at that end. The cherubim are to be shaped out of the mercy seat itself, at its two ends.

L.19: And make one cherub at the end on this [side] and one cherub at the end on that [side]; of the mercy seat you shall make the cherubim, on its two ends.

R.19: Place a cherub at each end of the lid. Make the cherubim and the lid all from one piece of gold.

decisions.choice: from the mercy seat: of one piece with it
decisions.reason: "From the mercy seat" means that the cherubim are made out of the same piece of gold as the mercy seat, as "hammered work" in verse 18 implies.

records.source: וְהָי֣וּ הַכְּרֻבִים֩ פֹּרְשֵׂ֨י כְנָפַ֜יִם לְמַ֗עְלָה סֹכְכִ֤ים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם֙ עַל־הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת וּפְנֵיהֶ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־אָחִ֑יו אֶל־הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת יִהְי֖וּ פְּנֵ֥י הַכְּרֻבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And will be the cherubim spreading out wings upward, covering with their wings over the mercy seat, and their faces each to his brother; toward the mercy seat will be [the] faces of the cherubim.
pieces: The cherubim are to spread their wings out above, sheltering the mercy seat with their wings. They are to face one another, with their faces turned toward the mercy seat.

L.20: And the cherubim shall be spreading out [their] wings upward, covering the mercy seat with their wings, and their faces each toward his brother; toward the mercy seat shall be the faces of the cherubim.

R.20: The cherubim must spread their wings upward over the lid, sheltering it. They must face each other and turn their faces toward the lid.

decisions.choice: covering: sheltering, screening
decisions.reason: The verb means to screen or shelter, as a bird covers with its wings. The cherubim's wings overshadow the mercy seat (1 Kings 8:7; Hebrews 9:5).

decisions.choice: each toward his brother: facing one another
decisions.reason: "A man to his brother" is a Hebrew way of saying "one another", used here of the two figures.

decisions.choice: faces toward the mercy seat: looking down at the lid
decisions.reason: The two cherubim face each other and look down toward the mercy seat between them.

records.source: וְנָתַתָּ֧ אֶת־הַכַּפֹּ֛רֶת עַל־הָאָרֹ֖ן מִלְמָ֑עְלָה וְאֶל־הָ֣אָרֹ֔ן תִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־הָ֣עֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶתֵּ֖ן אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And you will put the mercy seat on the ark from to above, and into the ark you will put the testimony which I will give to you.
pieces: The mercy seat is to go on top of the ark, and inside the ark you are to put the testimony I will give you.

L.21: And you shall put the mercy seat on the ark, on top, and into the ark you shall put the testimony which I will give you.

R.21: Put the lid on top of the ark, and put the covenant tablets that I will give you inside the ark.

decisions.choice: into the ark ... the testimony: the command of verse 16 repeated
decisions.reason: The repetition joins the two things that belong together: the tablets of the covenant inside the ark and the mercy seat over them. When the tabernacle is set up, Moses puts the testimony in the ark and then sets the mercy seat on it (40:20).

decisions.choice: from above: on top
decisions.reason: The mercy seat lies on the top of the ark as its lid.

records.source: וְנוֹעַדְתִּ֣י לְךָ֮ שָׁם֒ וְדִבַּרְתִּ֨י אִתְּךָ֜ מֵעַ֣ל הַכַּפֹּ֗רֶת מִבֵּין֙ שְׁנֵ֣י הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־אֲרֹ֣ן הָעֵדֻ֑ת אֵ֣ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֲצַוֶּ֛ה אוֹתְךָ֖ אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And I will meet you there and I will speak with you from above the mercy seat, from between [the] two cherubim which [are] on [the] ark of the testimony, all that I will command you to [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: I will meet with you there. I will speak with you from above the mercy seat, from the space between the two cherubim on the ark of the testimony, and give you every command meant for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.22: And I will meet with you there, and I will speak with you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim which [are] on the ark of the testimony, all that I will command you for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.22: I will meet with you there, above the lid, between the two cherubim on the ark that holds the covenant tablets. From there I will tell you all the commands you are to give the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: I will meet: meet by appointment
decisions.reason: The verb means to meet at an appointed place or time. The "tent of meeting" takes its name from the same root (27:21; 29:42-43, where God says "there I will meet with you").

decisions.choice: I will speak with you from above the mercy seat: the place where God speaks
decisions.reason: The space above the mercy seat, between the cherubim, is where God makes himself present and speaks. Numbers 7:89 tells how Moses heard the voice speaking to him from there.

decisions.choice: the ark of the testimony: the chest that holds the tablets
decisions.reason: The ark is named for what it holds, the tablets of the testimony (verse 16). The same ark is called "the ark of the covenant" elsewhere (Numbers 10:33; Deuteronomy 10:8).

decisions.choice: the ark that holds the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: Readable says "the ark that holds the covenant tablets" for "the ark of the testimony" (verse 16). It also says "the commands you are to give", which is what "command you to the Israelites" means.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ שֻׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּוֹ֙ וְאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And you will make a table [of] woods of acacia, two cubits its length, and a cubit its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height.
pieces: Make a table of acacia wood, {{units:about 3 feet|2 cubits}} long, {{units:about 1 1/2 feet|1 cubit}} wide and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} high.

L.23: And you shall make a table [of] acacia wood; 2 cubits [shall be] its length, and 1 cubit its breadth, and 1 1/2 cubits its height.

R.23: Make a table out of acacia wood. It must be {{units:about 3 feet|2 cubits}} long, {{units:about 1 1/2 feet|1 cubit}} wide, and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}} high.

decisions.choice: a table: the table for the bread of the Presence
decisions.reason: The table holds the bread of the Presence (verse 30) and stands in the holy place, on the north side, across from the lampstand (26:35). Its size, about 36 by 18 by 27 inches (about 90 by 45 by 68 centimeters), is given in cubits (see verse 10).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 3 feet|2 cubits}} ... {{units:about 1 1/2 feet|1 cubit}} ... {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|1 1/2 cubits}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, the measures are given in feet with the original cubits in the units setting; Literal keeps cubits.

records.heading: The table

records.source: וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹת֖וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ לּ֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And you will overlay it [with] gold pure, and you will make for it a molding of gold all around.
pieces: Overlay it with pure gold, and give it a gold molding all the way around.

L.24: And you shall overlay it [with] pure gold, and make for it a molding of gold all around.

R.24: Cover it with pure gold, and put a gold border all around it.

decisions.choice: overlay ... molding: as for the ark
decisions.reason: The table is finished the same way as the ark (verse 11): overlaid with pure gold and given a gold molding around it.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ לּ֥וֹ מִסְגֶּ֛רֶת טֹ֖פַח סָבִ֑יב וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ זֵר־זָהָ֛ב לְמִסְגַּרְתּ֖וֹ סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And you will make for it a rim [of] a handbreadth all around, and you will make a molding of gold for its rim all around.
pieces: Give it a frame {{units:about 3 inches|a handbreadth}} wide on every side, with a gold molding all around the frame.

L.25: And you shall make for it a frame of a handbreadth all around, and you shall make a molding of gold for its frame all around.

R.25: Make a frame {{units:about 3 inches|a handbreadth}} wide all around it, and put a gold border around the frame.

decisions.choice: frame: a rim or a band joining the legs
decisions.reason: The word means something that encloses: a rim or frame. It may be a raised rim around the tabletop, or a band of wood joining the legs below the top to brace them. Verse 27 places the rings for the poles near it, beside the legs, which fits a frame between the legs.

decisions.choice: handbreadth: the width of a hand across the four fingers, about 3 inches (7.5 centimeters)
decisions.reason: The handbreadth was a sixth of a cubit and the smallest common measure of length.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 3 inches|a handbreadth}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern measure by default, and the units setting shows the original "a handbreadth". Literal keeps "handbreadth".

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ אַרְבַּ֖ע טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב וְנָתַתָּ֙ אֶת־הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And you will make for it four rings of gold, and you will put the rings on the four corners which [belong] to its four feet.
pieces: Make it four rings of gold and set them at the four corners, one by each of its four legs.

L.26: And you shall make for it four rings of gold, and put the rings on the four corners which [belong] to its four feet.

R.26: Make four gold rings and put one at each corner, beside each of its four legs.

decisions.choice: the four corners which belong to its four feet: the corners where the legs are
decisions.reason: The rings are placed at the corners of the table, at the tops of the legs. "Feet" here means the legs of the table.

decisions.choice: legs
decisions.reason: The word is "feet"; for a table Balanced and Readable say "legs". Literal keeps "feet".

records.source: לְעֻמַּת֙ הַמִּסְגֶּ֔רֶת תִּהְיֶ֖יןָ הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת לְבָתִּ֣ים לְבַדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת־הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן׃
records.gloss: Close to the rim will be the rings, for holders for poles to carry the table.
pieces: Place the rings near the frame; they will hold the poles by which the table is carried.

L.27: Close to the frame the rings shall be, as holders for poles, to carry the table.

R.27: Put the rings near the frame. The poles for carrying the table will go through them.

decisions.choice: holders: housings for the poles
decisions.reason: The word means a place or housing. The rings serve as sleeves to hold the carrying poles.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ אֶת־הַבַּדִּים֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָ֑ב וְנִשָּׂא־בָ֖ם אֶת־הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן׃
records.gloss: And you will make the poles [of] woods of acacia, and you will overlay them [with] gold, and will be carried by them the table.
pieces: Make the poles from acacia wood and overlay them with gold. The table will be carried with them.

L.28: And you shall make the poles [of] acacia wood, and overlay them [with] gold, and the table shall be carried by them.

R.28: Make the poles out of acacia wood, and cover them with gold. Use them to carry the table.

decisions.choice: the poles ... the table shall be carried: as with the ark
decisions.reason: Like the ark, the table is carried on poles and not handled (verses 13-14; Numbers 4:7-8, 15).

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ קְּעָרֹתָ֜יו וְכַפֹּתָ֗יו וּקְשׂוֹתָיו֙ וּמְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will make its dishes and its pans and its jugs and its bowls which will be poured out with them; [of] gold pure you will make them.
pieces: Make its dishes, its pans, its jars and its bowls, which are used for pouring out drink offerings; make them of pure gold.

L.29: And you shall make its dishes and its pans and its jugs and its bowls with which [drink offerings] are poured out; [of] pure gold you shall make them.

R.29: Make its plates, small pans, jars, and bowls out of pure gold. Some of them will be used for pouring out drink offerings.

decisions.choice: dishes, pans, jugs and bowls: the table's vessels
decisions.reason: The exact shape of each vessel is not certain. The first are dishes or platters, perhaps for the bread. The second, named from the word for the palm of the hand, are small pans or ladles; such a pan is filled with incense in Numbers 7:14 (compare Leviticus 24:7). The last two are jugs and bowls for liquids.

decisions.choice: which will be poured out with them: vessels for drink offerings
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for pouring out a drink offering of wine (29:40-41; Numbers 28:7). Numbers 4:7 calls these "the jugs for the drink offering". The clause most likely describes the jugs and bowls, not all four vessels.

decisions.choice: drink offerings
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "which will be poured out with them". All levels name what is poured, as Numbers 4:7 does; Literal brackets it. Readable says "some of them", since the clause most likely refers to the jugs and bowls (m2).

records.source: וְנָתַתָּ֧ עַֽל־הַשֻּׁלְחָ֛ן לֶ֥חֶם פָּנִ֖ים לְפָנַ֥י תָּמִֽיד׃פ
records.gloss: And you will put on the table bread of face before me continually.
pieces: On the table you are to set the bread of the Presence, to lie before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} continually.

L.30: And you shall put on the table bread of the face before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} continually.

R.30: Always keep the bread of the Presence on the table in front of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: bread of the face: bread set before God's presence
decisions.reason: "Face" here means presence: the bread lies before God. Leviticus 24:5-9 gives the details: twelve loaves, set out in two rows, renewed every Sabbath, and eaten by the priests in a holy place. It is also called "the regular bread" (Numbers 4:7).

decisions.choice: continually: always, without a break
decisions.reason: The bread is never removed without fresh bread taking its place (Leviticus 24:8).

decisions.choice: the bread of the Presence
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the bread of the Presence" for "the bread of the face", which Literal keeps.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ מְנֹרַ֖ת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה תֵּעָשֶׂ֤ה הַמְּנוֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה יִהְיֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And you will make a lampstand [of] gold pure; hammered work will be made the lampstand, its base and its shaft; its cups, its bulbs and its blossoms from it will be.
pieces: Make a lampstand of pure gold, hammered out. Its base and its shaft, its cups, its buds and its blossoms are to form one piece with it.

L.31: And you shall make a lampstand of pure gold; [of] hammered work the lampstand shall be made, its base and its shaft; its cups, its bulbs and its blossoms shall be from it.

R.31: Make a lampstand out of pure gold. Hammer the whole thing from one piece of gold: its base, its center stem, and its cups, buds, and blossoms.

decisions.choice: lampstand: a stand holding seven oil lamps
decisions.reason: The lampstand is made like a tree: a central stem with three branches on each side, decorated with flower shapes (verses 32-36), holding seven lamps (verse 37). It stood on the south side of the holy place, across from the table (26:35), and its lamps were tended every evening and morning (27:20-21; 30:7-8).

decisions.choice: base and shaft: the foot of the lampstand and its central stem
decisions.reason: The first word means the thigh or lower part, here the base. The second is the word used for the branches in verse 32 (a reed or stalk), here the central stem.

decisions.choice: cups, bulbs and blossoms: decorations shaped like parts of a flower
decisions.reason: The cups are shaped like almond flowers (verse 33). The second word means a knob or round bulb, perhaps the swelling at the base of a flower; the third means a blossom or open flower. The exact shapes are not certain.

decisions.choice: buds
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "bulbs" for the round knobs; Balanced and Readable say "buds", the closest familiar part of a flower (m3).

records.heading: The lampstand

records.source: וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה׀קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And six branches [will be] going out from its sides: three branches of [the] lampstand from its one side, and three branches of [the] lampstand from its second side.
pieces: Six branches are to come out from the sides of the lampstand: from one side three of its branches, and from the other side three.

L.32: And six branches [shall be] going out from its sides: three branches of the lampstand from its one side, and three branches of the lampstand from its second side.

R.32: Six branches will come out of the sides of the lampstand, three on each side.

decisions.choice: branches: arms of the lampstand
decisions.reason: The word means a reed or stalk. It names the six arms that curve out from the central stem, three on each side.

records.source: שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בַּקָּנֶ֥ה הָאֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן־הַמְּנֹרָֽה׃
records.gloss: Three cups made like almond [blossoms] on the one branch, a bulb and a blossom, and three cups made like almond [blossoms] on the one branch, a bulb and a blossom; so for [the] six branches the [ones] going out from the lampstand.
pieces: One branch is to have three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with a bud and a blossom, and the next branch three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with a bud and a blossom. It is to be the same for all six branches that come out of the lampstand.

L.33: Three cups made like almond [blossoms] on the one branch, a bulb and a blossom; and three cups made like almond [blossoms] on the other branch, a bulb and a blossom; so for the six branches going out from the lampstand.

R.33: Each of the six branches that come out of the lampstand will have three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with buds and blossoms.

decisions.choice: made like almond blossoms: shaped like the flower of the almond tree
decisions.reason: The word comes from the name of the almond tree, which blooms first in the year. Almonds also bloom on Aaron's staff when God chooses him (Numbers 17), and Jeremiah 1:11-12 plays on the almond's name, which sounds like "watching".

decisions.choice: a bulb and a blossom: the parts of each cup
alternatives: a bulb and a blossom beside each set of cups
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely describes what each cup is made of, a round base and open petals, rather than further decorations alongside the cups.

decisions.choice: Each of the six branches
decisions.reason: Readable states once what the Hebrew says branch by branch, since all six are alike.

records.source: וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And on the lampstand [will be] four cups made like almond [blossoms], its bulbs and its blossoms.
pieces: On the lampstand itself there are to be four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with its buds and blossoms.

L.34: And on the lampstand [shall be] four cups made like almond [blossoms], its bulbs and its blossoms.

R.34: The center stem of the lampstand will have four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with buds and blossoms.

decisions.choice: on the lampstand: on the central stem
decisions.reason: Here "the lampstand" means its central stem, as distinct from the branches. It has four cups, one more than each branch.

decisions.choice: The center stem
decisions.reason: Readable names the part of the lampstand meant (m1).

records.source: וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּחַת־שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֨שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן־הַמְּנֹרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And a bulb under two of the branches from it, and a bulb under two of the branches from it, and a bulb under two of the branches from it, for [the] six branches the [ones] going out from the lampstand.
pieces: There is to be a bud under each pair of branches that come out of it: one bud beneath each of the three pairs, for the six branches that come out of the lampstand.

L.35: And a bulb under two of the branches from it, and a bulb under two of the branches from it, and a bulb under two of the branches from it, for the six branches going out from the lampstand.

R.35: Put a bud under each pair of branches, where they come out of the center stem. Do this for all three pairs.

decisions.choice: a bulb under two of the branches: a knob where each pair of branches leaves the stem
decisions.reason: Each pair of branches, one on each side, comes out of the stem at a knob. Three such knobs on the stem account for the six branches. These may be three of the four cups' bulbs on the stem (verse 34).

decisions.choice: a bud under each pair of branches
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the clause three times, once for each pair. Balanced and Readable say it once and add "each of the three pairs"; Literal keeps the repetition.

records.source: כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה יִהְי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: Their bulbs and their branches from it will be, all of it hammered work one [of] gold pure.
pieces: Their buds and their branches are to be part of it, the whole of it a single hammered piece of pure gold.

L.36: Their bulbs and their branches shall be from it; all of it one hammered work of pure gold.

R.36: The buds and branches must all be part of the lampstand. The whole lampstand must be hammered out of one piece of pure gold.

decisions.choice: one hammered work: beaten out of a single piece
decisions.reason: Nothing is soldered on; the whole lampstand with its branches and decorations is beaten from one piece of gold, like the cherubim and the mercy seat (verses 18-19).

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת־נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וְהֶֽעֱלָה֙ אֶת־נֵ֣רֹתֶ֔יהָ וְהֵאִ֖יר עַל־עֵ֥בֶר פָּנֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And you will make its lamps, seven, and one will set up its lamps, and it will give light on [the] side of its face.
pieces: Make seven lamps for it. The lamps are to be mounted so that their light falls on the space before the lampstand.

L.37: And you shall make its lamps, seven; and [one] shall set up its lamps, and it shall give light on the side in front of it.

R.37: Make seven lamps for the lampstand. Place them so that they light up the area in front of it.

decisions.choice: its lamps, seven: seven small oil lamps
decisions.reason: The lamps were small clay-style vessels, here of gold, holding oil and a wick. They sat on the tops of the stem and the six branches.

decisions.choice: one will set up: the lamps are set in place, or lit
decisions.reason: The verb, "he will lift up", has no stated subject; it means the lamps are set up, perhaps also lit (the same verb is used of lighting the lamps in 30:8 and Numbers 8:2-3). Aaron and his sons tend the lamps (27:21).

decisions.choice: give light on the side of its face: shine on the area in front of it
decisions.reason: The lamps are turned so that their light falls on the space in front of the lampstand (Numbers 8:2).

records.source: וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And its tongs and its fire pans [will be of] gold pure.
pieces: Its tongs and its fire pans are to be of pure gold.

L.38: And its tongs and its fire pans [shall be of] pure gold.

R.38: The tongs for trimming the wicks and the small pans that go with them must also be made of pure gold.

decisions.choice: tongs and fire pans: tools for tending the lamps
decisions.reason: The tongs were used to trim or adjust the wicks. The pans most likely held the burnt pieces of wick and ash; the same word is used for the pans that carry coals (27:3; Leviticus 10:1).

decisions.choice: for trimming the wicks ... that go with them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the tongs were for and links the pans to them (m1). "Also" connects them with the pure gold of the lampstand.

records.source: כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַכֵּלִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: [Of] a talent [of] gold pure one will make it, all the articles the these.
pieces: The lampstand and all these utensils are to be made from {{units:about 75 pounds|a talent}} of pure gold.

L.39: [Of] a talent of pure gold [one] shall make it, [with] all these articles.

R.39: Use {{units:about 75 pounds|a talent}} of pure gold to make the lampstand and all these tools.

decisions.choice: talent: a weight of 3,000 shekels, about 75 pounds (34 kilograms)
decisions.reason: The talent was the largest common weight. 38:24-26 shows that it was 3,000 shekels of the sanctuary, and a shekel weighed about two-fifths of an ounce (11.5 grams). The figure is approximate.

decisions.choice: one will make it, all these articles: the lampstand and its tools together
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject, and "it" is the lampstand. The talent of gold covers the lampstand and all its utensils together.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 75 pounds|a talent}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in pounds by default, rounded, with "about"; the units setting shows the original "a talent". Literal keeps "talent".

records.source: וּרְאֵ֖ה וַעֲשֵׂ֑ה בְּתַ֨בְנִיתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה מָרְאֶ֖ה בָּהָֽר׃ס
records.gloss: And see and make [them] in their pattern which you [are] being shown on the mountain.
pieces: Take care to make them by the pattern you are being shown on the mountain.

L.40: And see, and make [them] by their pattern which you are being shown on the mountain.

R.40: Be careful to make everything exactly like the plan I am showing you on the mountain.

decisions.choice: see and make: see to it that you make
decisions.reason: "See" here is a call to take care: Moses must make sure the work follows what he has been shown.

decisions.choice: their pattern which you are being shown on the mountain: the design God gives
decisions.reason: The verse repeats verse 9: everything is to follow the pattern God shows Moses on the mountain (compare 26:30; 27:8). Hebrews 8:5 quotes this verse, and Acts 7:44 refers to it.

decisions.choice: I am showing you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "you are being shown". God is the one showing, as verse 9 says ("I am showing you"), so Readable says "I". It also says "plan" for "pattern", as in verse 9.
